arm-linux-cross UNIT SET -- READ THIS BEFORE USING THE BIN TARBALL
==================================================================
Added 2026-09-11.  This file is NOT mirrored inside any published tarball, so it
can be corrected later without making an already-shipped artifact disagree with
it.  VERSION.txt in this directory is byte-identical (md5
18d45fee3024bdf4a9d731e604f21897) to the copy inside the v58 cross bin tarball
and is therefore left exactly as it shipped.

THIS DIRECTORY IS A POINTER, NOT A SECOND TARBALL
-------------------------------------------------
This target ships a CROSS compiler: an x86_64-linux binary that emits 32-bit
arm-linux code.  Its TARGET is arm-linux, so it consumes exactly the same unit
set as the native arm-linux compiler.  Nothing arm-linux-cross-specific exists
and nothing here needs to be downloaded twice.  Get the units from:

  dist/arm-linux/vibepascal-v54-arm-linux-units-full.tar.gz
      82757332 bytes
      md5    6e92ffab6cb292c65dc0dc393a487164
      sha256 aca16ac314da1730e3253c71807d2a8249fc4e31c5f54f98a5a2438afa855030
      3496 files flat in units/arm-linux/: 1646 .ppu (99 RTL + 1547 package),
      1600 .o, 249 .rsj, 1 .inc.
      Full writeup, including why the units say v54 and the compiler says v58:
      dist/arm-linux/UNITS.txt

  Do NOT use dist/arm-linux/vibepascal-v54-arm-linux-units.tar.gz.  It is still
  published and still valid, but it is the RTL and nothing else (204 files), so
  it can build a program that uses SysUtils and Classes and cannot build one
  that uses fpjson.

YOU ALSO NEED CROSS BINUTILS, AND THIS IS THE PART THAT BITES
--------------------------------------------------------------
The compiler binary is x86_64.  Left to itself it calls YOUR HOST's assembler
and linker, and a host x86_64 ld cannot link ARM objects.  Measured here on the
published bytes, with the unit set present and correct:

  ./bin/ppcrossarm -n -FU. -Fuunits/arm-linux -Flunits/arm-linux pkgtest.pas

  /usr/bin/ld.bfd: skipping incompatible ./units/arm-linux/varutils.o when
                   searching for ./units/arm-linux/varutils.o
  /usr/bin/ld.bfd: cannot find ./units/arm-linux/varutils.o: No such file or directory
  pkgtest.pas(18,1) Error: Error while linking
  pkgtest.pas(18,1) Fatal: There were 1 errors compiling module, stopping
  rc=1

That message names a unit .o and reads like a broken or incomplete unit set.  It
is not.  The units are fine; the LINKER is the wrong architecture.  This is
intrinsic to cross compilation -- it is not a qemu artifact and it happens on
every host.  The internal linker is NOT a way around it: -Xi was tried and fell
through to /usr/bin/ld.bfd and failed identically.

So install armhf binutils and point the compiler at them with -XP:

  sudo apt-get install -y binutils-arm-linux-gnueabihf     (Debian/Ubuntu)

  ./bin/ppcrossarm -n -FU. -Fuunits/arm-linux -Flunits/arm-linux \
                   -XParm-linux-gnueabihf- pkgtest.pas

The ABI must match: this compiler is built -dFPC_ARMHF (ARM EABI5, HARD float),
so it needs the gnueabihf binutils, not the soft-float armel ones.  No sysroot
and no ARM libc are required -- the output is statically linked.

Note for anyone comparing with dist/arm-linux/UNITS.txt: the command documented
THERE has no -XP, and that is correct for that file.  The native ppcarm running
on a real ARM board finds a native as/ld and needs no prefix.  -XP is a
CROSS-compiler requirement.

WHAT WAS MEASURED, ON THE PUBLISHED BYTES, IN AN EMPTY DIRECTORY
-----------------------------------------------------------------
  * vibepascal-v58-dedf242c69-arm-linux-cross-bin.tar.gz re-downloaded
    UNAUTHENTICATED from raw.githubusercontent.com: HTTP 200, 1768165 bytes,
    md5 0f35c1601c2441a69977e7b9baa2b6d6, identical to the local copy.
    Extracted bin/ppcrossarm md5 5e3d9ba2d978db06b31a1a15c37244d9 -- matches the
    md5 its OWN VERSION.txt declares.
  * The 82 MB unit tarball was NOT re-downloaded.  Published-vs-local was
    settled with the GitHub contents API instead: the published blob sha1
    7cdc30407935dbad3fcc63dd5e4c9eaefc4ae2c8 equals `git hash-object` on the
    local file, sizes 82757332 both sides.
  * Compiler identity: -iV 3.3.1, -iD 2026/09/11, -iTP arm, -iSP x86_64.  The
    last two are the point: TARGET arm, HOST x86_64.
  * EXTRACT TO RUNNING PROGRAM, from the published bytes only, both tarballs into
    one empty directory, -n so this host's installed FPC could supply nothing:

        program pkgtest;
        {$mode objfpc}{$H+}
        uses SysUtils, Classes, fpjson;    <-- fpjson is a PACKAGE unit, on
                                               purpose: an RTL-only unit set
                                               passes a hello-world smoke and
                                               fails here.
        ...

    rc=0, artifact "ELF 32-bit LSB executable, ARM, EABI5 version 1 (SYSV),
    statically linked", and it RAN under qemu-arm-static:

        HELLO vibepascal arm-linux-cross 2 { "target" : "arm-linux-cross", "nativeint" : 4 }

  * NEGATIVE CONTROL, scored on its message TEXT and not on its exit code
    (an exit code is not a reason -- the wrong flag returns rc=1 too):
    with units/ moved aside,
        hello.pas(1,15) Fatal: Can't find unit system used by hello
    So the run above could have failed, and did not.

  Proof tree: ~/src/vibepascal-slices/armcross/ (README.txt has the exact
  reproduce command).

NOT PROVEN HERE: qemu-user is an emulator.  It runs the real shipped bytes and
real ARM encodings, so codegen and RTL defects do surface, but it is not a
Raspberry Pi.  Nobody has run this compiler's output on physical ARM silicon.
